reasoning_content:
The reason memory dropped to 123MB during the build and then recovered was either a GC/space issue or the OOM killer. The 7.6GB machine physically cannot handle the 3-way simultaneous Angular build — the peak build-time footprint (each Angular app's build requires about 1.5–2GB) exceeds the available capacity.

At this point, I've spent quite a lot of time on the dev server orchestration part. Let me step back and think:

1. The installation itself (`just up`) is **complete**: all 10 containers are running and healthy, the backend is built and running (health UP), sample data is seeded, Keycloak realm is imported with working login, and the proxy is routing.
2. The three Angular dev servers **all build and run successfully** — I've verified app=200, cms=200, boards=200 individually, and the proxy routes correctly too.
3. The only issue is **simultaneously** running all 3 on this 7.6GB machine — a limitation of the environment resources, not an installation defect.

Let me check the current state of the last serve attempt — one of the builds may have completed. Let me wait a bit more before deciding.

Actually, I realized I should first check whether the build is even making progress. Memory is stable at around 540MB, and the servers still haven't started. Let me check.

action.command: echo "t=$(date +%H:%M:%S)"; tail -8 /tmp/serve-last.log; echo "=== build procs ==="; ps aux | grep -E "run-executor" | grep -v grep | awk '{printf "pid=%s rss=%sMB cpu=%s%%\n",$2,int($6/1024),$3}' | head; echo "=== logs ==="; for f in app cms boards; do echo "--$f--"; tail -2 /workspace/.urbo/workspace/logs/$f.log; done; free -m | sed -n '2p'
